messages:
olivia: Quick heads-up — I'm drafting a docs PR that covers an "offload proxy" pattern for air-gapped installs. The idea: the installer stays air-gapped, but a customer-run proxy (in a DMZ) can accept signing requests and forward them to an HSM in a controlled, audited way. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4321 :eyes:

matt: Nice. A couple clarifying Qs: is the proxy expected to run in the customer's public subnet with NAT? or in the VPC but with limited egress? We should be explicit about network placement and port requirements.

priya: Important: we must call out the threat model and that private keys never leave the HSM. Offload proxy should only send signing operations (PIN/PKCS11 transactions) and should log ops. Also add guidance for mTLS + client cert rotation.

kevin: For install UX, recommend a minimal preflight checklist:
- proxy host reachable from installer (HTTPs port 8443)
- client cert uploaded to proxy via airgap bundle
- HSM reachable from proxy on PKCS11 port (usually 5696)
- health endpoint /v1/health returns 200 and shows HSM status

olivia: Thanks — I'll add a short network matrix and a minimal example of the proxy config. Thinking of including an SDK example for signing through the proxy (node + curl) so customers can copy/paste into their apps. Any objections to showing a token-based auth snippet?

priya: Token-based auth is fine if we emphasize short TTLs + rotational flow. Add an example of using KMS to encrypt the token in the airgap bundle rather than embedding raw creds. Also call out auditing: "x-request-id" header and request tracing.

matt: For the network details, here's a tiny sample to include in docs (we can put in a code block):

```
# proxy firewall rules (customer DMZ)
# allow installer -> proxy
- from: installer-cidr
  to: proxy-ip
  proto: tcp
  port: 8443
# allow proxy -> hsm
- from: proxy-ip
  to: hsm-ip
  proto: tcp
  port: 5696
```

kevin: Also add a preflight command people can run on the proxy host: 
```
curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key https://localhost:8443/v1/health
```

olivia: Adding a concise Node snippet for signing via the proxy. Will label it "example only — adapt for your security policy".

```
// node example: sign via offload proxy (mTLS + short token)
const https = require('https');
const payload = Buffer.from('important-data');
const options = {
  hostname: 'proxy.example.com',
  port: 8443,
  path: '/v1/sign',
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/octet-stream',
    'Authorization': 'Bearer short-lived-token',
    'x-request-id': 'req-' + Date.now()
  },
  key: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/private/client.key'),
  cert: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/certs/client.pem'),
  ca: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/certs/proxy-ca.pem')
};
const req = https.request(options, (res) => {
  let chunks = [];
  res.on('data', (d) => chunks.push(d));
  res.on('end', () => {
    const sig = Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('base64');
    console.log('signature:', sig);
  });
});
req.write(payload);
req.end();
```

olivia: I'll push the draft PR tonight. Plan: initial sections (overview, threat model, preflight checklist, proxy config, SDK snippets) and a short troubleshooting table. Anyone want to pair-review tomorrow morning?

matt: I can do a quick pass after standup (09:30 PT) — will check network matrix and wording.

kevin: I'll add the health-check example and a systemd unit fragment for running the proxy.

priya: I'll review security bits — especially token guidance and audit section. If we can link to the HSM operator runbook that would be great.

docs-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4321 — draft added to "airgap-offload-proxy". reviewers: @matt @priya @kevin

olivia: Awesome — thanks all. I'll also add an explicit "do not": do not copy HSM private keys into the airgap bundle. Put that in bold and a callout box. :warning: 

matt: +1 :thumbsup:

kevin: FYI I hit a tiny installer UX quirk — when the proxy CA bundle is >4kb the current CLI rejects it. I'll open a tiny bug and link it in the PR.

olivia: Please do and link it. Will wait for those two small fixes before merging.
